reviews.text: Incorrect Species. I’ve noticed recently that some species (Such as Carrion Crow and Hooded Crow) are the same species in the app whereas on all other bird ID sites and apps they are listed as separate species. This is a problem cause it messes with peoples Birda Life List and Life List on other apps, making them different and could cause confusion
Earth birds. Good job
Takes your info before telling you how much it costs. Also it's an annual charge so be prepared to pay for a whole year at once before getting to try it.

What am I missing?. I tried to log my first bird, a mountain chickadee, and it identified it as a crow at first. Also I find it confusing that you give what % likely it is. It only gave me 12% likely for a second photo I took but other apps just accurately identified the bird.

pictures become blurry. i love the app and the concept, bird watching is one of my top hobbies. unfortunately when i use the AI identification camera it lowers the quality of the pictures i take to such a degree the AI can’t identify a bird from a previously crystal clear picture. hoping this gets fixed cause i can see myself using this app regularly and trying to “collect” all the birds around my area :)
Phenomenal. Phenomenal bird app

Great app. Amazing app for community birding, sharing photos, and logging birds into the app. Awesome app overall, and I have a few suggestions for it. First, when I upload my eBird data to Birda, It doesn’t give me any badges for all the birds I’ve found. If you can also link that to the images I uploaded to eBird that would be great too.
Fun. I love birds

Not my thing. Beware! It’s essentially a knockoff of a seriously scientific app that is available at no cost. This app will take and take your money and so far despite several attempts, I’m finding it impossible to cancel.

I like the idea, needs improvement.. I’ve been using the paid version of the app for about a month or two now, and in its current state I’m switching to Merlin. 

1) the photo ID of the app is more often wrong than not. What made me decide to move away from
The app was realizing I use Google search to identify the birds than I do the app.

2) the UI interface is a bit clunky, not a deal breaker but can be frustrating when you’re sweaty, the middle of the woods trying to identify the same bird the photo ID got wrong 3 times in a row.

With that said, I understand the app is in its infancy and everything costs money. So I’m not recommending that you shouldn’t give the app a go or support the business, but for my personal use, its not worth it.
Can’t identify pictures. Have to have location on, and there’s no option to identify a bird that isn’t at my physical location.
Stuck in challenge screen. This app is buggy. Doesn’t do anything but offer the challenge.

If you want a Facebook-like birding experience…. Disappointed that you have to create an account and agree to a subscription to even SEE the app and what it may or may not do. If you want actual bird maps and tracking your list for free, use Merlin and eBird. If you’re looking to socialize, give away your location and personal information, and sort-of bird, then this app is for you.

7 Day free trial. Wanted to try the app and was super excited about it, I’ll update my receive once I do. I just found it super dishonest that Birda offers a “7 Day free trial.” And immediately removes $20.56 from your account. Is this included towards my yearly if so the yearly isn’t $30 it’s $50? Since when is a “Free Trial.” Not free ? Questions that require answers.
Skip, not free. Not free in any capacity. Join me in 1 star rating apps that deceives you into believing it’s free and then locking every feature behind a paywall
Birda. Having fun!

Beware. They just want your money. You're told you'll be notified before the free trial ends, but no such notification ever comes. Instead, you're automatically charged and pushed into an annual plan, clearly relying on you forgetting. Even after canceling immediately, the charge for the full year remains. This is a predatory tactic designed to take your money regardless of the app's actual quality.

Waste of time. Nearly every picture you take or upload comes back with an error saying their AI cant figure out what bird it is, also impeccable yall care about “screen times” and being online yet youre using AI technology that is fueled by huge data centers burning water that can never be reused…interesting.
Bird watching. It helps you go outside and explore and learn new birds
Only free trial. So sick of these apps using ads that make them seem free. Don’t bother downloading- 7 day free trial only
Best all. I was looking for a childhood bird but never found it, then Birda app popped up in an ad, problem solved , than you
Love!. Very helpful app!
Not free. Says play for free but 2.99 a month but charges $35
Birds. This app is super helpful
Sound id. Needs sound id
Not free as advertised. Advertised as free and charges $36/year

Identification feature leaves a lot to be desired. Beware of the Ai identification feature, its performance is generally very poor. If you are new to birding and looking to use the app for identification rather than just logging sightings, I’d pass on this and use iNat or a field guide instead. There’s been many times where I’ve put a photo into the ID feature and it’s given me some crazy answer that was obviously inaccurate. I think it’s a fine app for tracking sightings, and I like the ease with which you can upload photos and join challenges. However, be wary and know that the ID feature is not good.
Wow!. One of the best birding apps in the world
Worth the sub. Tons of features including bird sounds. Great for logging sightings and identification.

Confused about options. Using this with my kids. It’s fun, but I can’t understand why their app has different buttons than mine. I have feed, challenges, discover, and profile. My son has explore, community, challenges, and profile. Please help me figure this out!

Nagware?. I just downloaded it to my iPhone and was basically forced to sign up for a 7 day free trial. That’s really annoying. I read that’s for Birda+ but should that be an option for users to consider later?
"free" trial instantly charged my card for $44.47. Rip off! The app seems cool enough but that trial instantly charging me is BS
Too easy. This is not what I anticipated you have to be in the place where you see the bird in order to put the location in and the birds they’re providing me with I see on a regular basis

Best birding app in the word #2. As you know I love this app! I love to share my photography! But do you think you could add more slots for photos? You don’t have to though if you’re busy! it’s already an amazing app!

Gave it a shot. While I appreciate the concept, the app is slow and contains bugs. Setting the duration of a walk/trip is pointless as it will change by itself and say it lasted seconds. When you try to fix it, it gets confused and thinks you’re time traveling. Furthermore, some birds won’t show, lists don’t seem to organize by date but rather posting date, uploading images takes a while, and the community board left me longing for customization. For example, I wish I could select to see just the posts from my state and not all the way to Canada. It feels more like a posting board than a bird app.
Nope. Be careful! They offer you a 7 day free trial but charge you $39 regardless.
Love it, but post upload is slow. I love the community and the tools. -1 star for: I don't know if it is only me but the post upload is quite slow, usually takes like a minute to upload one image.
Boooo. Paywall, don’t download. Get Merlin.

Not as good as eBird or INaturalist. This app has a bad interface, poor ID tools, and is redundant. Also- the fact that there is a Birda+ paid option is upsetting. Citizen science and bird watching should NOT be a pay to play system. 

Overall, this app does absolutely nothing that INaturalist doesn’t do, and makes you pay for full features, which are free on iNat.

Fantastic!. Birda is exactly what I was looking for in a social birding app! If it didn’t exist I was about to make one myself. I love that I can like and comment on other’s photos and find photos of a certain bird by species. The challenges will get me out in nature more. 

There’s a few things that might make this app even better:

- Ability to change default email address 
- A forums feature to discuss birding topics like best camera gear, conservation efforts, etc. and make it searchable using AI.
- A feature similar to meetup.com or couchsurfing.com where users can connect with other nearby birders to plan birding trips together. I realize safety features would need to be added.

Really great idea. Love how this app keeps track of your logs, has some gamification, is oriented towards sharing photos instead of addition to lists. I’ve paid for the full version since I really want the app to do well. The big problem is responsiveness. It takes too long from tap to tap almost no matter where I am in the system. Other apps are basically instant but don’t have the fun and social aspect of Birda that is really like to be part of my birding experience.
I don’t like my name being broadcast to everyone. I would appreciate the app more if it allowed us to display a username instead of my full name.
Bird Id seems to fail on iOS 26. Used to be able to use photos to identify bird.

Features Broken. While I was enjoying the app, I now can’t seem to do a simple search to log a sighting. Maybe there is poor AI on the back end? In any case, I enter literally any text in the search box and nothing returns…just a blank white screen.
Misrepresentation. This App is NOT free!!! Liars!!!

I WISH I COULD GIVE THIS APP 0 STARS!!!!!!. First this app made my account password to be my login password to my iPad and it wouldn’t even let me select any pictures!Who ever made this app shame on you!

Add more challenges/daily missions. This birding app is awesome, but I feel like there’s so much you could add it would be a crime not to! Adding more challenges and daily missions would be awesome.. kind of like PokemonGo but for real birds!

Not as advertised. The whole reason I was excited about the app was the call identification shown in the video, when I bought the app however, that particular item is faded out and marked “coming soon”.
Ajo. Either bid
Better than fantasy football. I wish I could get my friends into birding. But they’d probably ruin it by making it a competition we could gamble on. So I may just keep this app to myself.
Excellent complement. Platform keeps improving and helps sustain motivation to share as much info as possible on state of bird populations everywhere

Great app. This app really is great. Me and my wife are having a contest to see who can log the most birds and having a blast doing it. The a.i. identification works really well and whole app is really intuitive and smooth and full of useful information.

Can't log proper kind of birds. This app doesn't let me log a bird when the bird is an invasive spiecies and not native in the area, which is
inconvenient and not accurate. I think we should be able to log a bird when we observe it, no matter what kind it is. It's really frustrating because I know exactly what kind, but the app it doesn't give me the option to select from a certain list.
Sound identification not available. The app says sound identification is not yet available. 🙁

Apps are made to cash in. Was wondering how this app would work, but like many apps, before you have a good feel it charges you. The seven days creeps up in our busy life. Tired of this. Now on principle will not use though got suckered into paying for a year.

Needs a way to mark wild/not wild. This game was advertised to me as Pokémon Go for bird watching. Yet, I’ve seen people complain that this is only for wild birds. Why not include a Not Wild check box for those people who want to track what they have seen? There are birds at the local zoo that I will never get a chance to see in the wild. Why should I be shamed for wanting to track that I’ve seen them?

Overall great app. Very enjoyable, but make sure you have a good camera.

Was awesome until…. They now require full access to your photo library. Not okay! Also, they don’t seem very responsive to the super users on the platform who have been having a lot of issues with people stealing photos lately.

Unbelievably invasive. I was really excited about this app until discovering that it requires you to give FULL ACCESS TO YOUR ENTIRE CAMERA ROLL in order to upload a photo of a bird. There’s absolutely no reason it can’t be limited to the photos you intend to upload to the app. Disgusting, invasive practices. Ruined any desire I had to use what could’ve been a really cool app.

Poor App Experience. In setting up app I granted access to only select photos from my photo album but it won’t allow me to do anything without giving full access to my camera and photo albums. Deleting and finding an app that works.

Disappointed :(. I was so excited to use the app but I was devastated that not every bird species was included in the identification search. Unfortunately it is a sad truth that domestic birds get released in places they shouldn’t and affect the local ecosystem as a result. I was excited to contribute to data collection of unusual sightings of domestic birds in the areas I frequent but they’re not even an option in the bird ID search. :(
Expensive. I’m NOT paying $36 to use a bird identifying app/social/game and give them my data and photos, too. Immediately deleting. I’ll stick with Merlin and eBird.

Great app.. I have two bird apps and this one is the stronger of the two. It works well, its bird identifier is pretty good. 
Would be even better if I could upload videos. 
Otherwise it’s a good app for identifying and lighting birds.
Have to pay to use. You have to pay for some basic app that’s just some fancy organizer. No sound ID. App is terrible to navigate. And looks like it was made by a 2 year old child.
AI Voiceover on ads. Maybe you’d flop less if you didn’t use AI, lazy bones

Not accessible very disappointing, N. Nothing like getting all excited for a new birdwatching app and then finding out the creators. Don’t care that you’re visually impaired. How about making this app accessible using voiceover. Cornell lab of ornithology makes their app Merlin bird ID perfectly accessible. I was looking forward to this app, however because it has a social aspect and I would love to connect with other birdwatchers. Alas, not for me as I have a vision impairment I guess visually impaired people can’t enjoy birds thanks a lot try contacting Apple for their free Developer tools to make apps accessible.
Seems like just for people in USA. Not much stuff in Hawaiʻi and I don’t see what the app does that inat and eBird doesn’t

Fun but major bugs. I’ve been using this alongside Ebird for over a year and I really enjoy the interface, challenges, badges and community engagement. Unfortunately the biggest issue is the logging and data. The database is often not correct with either bird names not up to date or certain bird species not even able to be selected in a given area requiring a very tedious logging procedure. I still enjoy using but will have to default to import data going forward because it’s just too time consuming otherwise.
Cancellation. I am having trouble cancelling my trial subscription, please help!?
birds. very nice community
One of the best. As a birdwatcher I enjoy being able to share my experiences and sightings with others, and this is the best app for that
Spotty AI. I love the idea of it but the picture ID just doesn't ever work. Like ever. You'll put in a picture of a sparrow and it will try to tell you it's a swan. How do you even get that?

What you should know.. The App is like twitter and instagram, but about birds. It’s great when you want to identify a bird, or are studying them. But it doesn’t work to well for older devices. Does what is should, works well, I would recommend it to all the bird lovers out there.

Doesn’t work at all. I installed and deleted this app within 3 minutes. It doesn’t work at all rendering it useless. It just tells me that my region isn’t yet supported even though I am North America like they state as a supported region. Fix your app or throw in the towel and find a new hobby.

Last update. This last update has made the app slower and now I am unable to load any photos in any of my feeds, or even my profile. No photos will load and that’s what I come for. To upload and view photos. I have tried restarting the app and restarting my phone and have attempted to come back several times to try and load the pages but with no success yet seeing any photos on Birda. Other that this I love this app and love the Birda community even more!

Love this app so much fun. When I updated it crashes when I try to log my birds please fix this Birda please. I love the app its quick it’s fun love it i see all kinds of bird I found a new habit thanks to Birda I love Birda my favorite app better then anything else
Great birding app!. This app is incredibly enjoyable! It’s an excellent way to keep track of the birds you’ve spotted, share your photos, and connect with like-minded bird enthusiasts.
Great social bird app. Birda has been a great beginner bird app it has a great community and if anyone can not identify a bird the community will always try to help
Amazing!. Such an amazing app for birdwatchers! Incredible!!!!!

Deceptive Practices. “Get Started, it’s Free”. Getting someone to go through the trouble of providing personal information and then at the end I have to provide payment information to enable a free trial? That’s cheap, tacky, common and deceptive. You can keep your app…
Love it. I have been on Birda not that long but it’s really good I like how the community helps you out when you can’t find out what the bird is so good job on it!:)
Nice app. Birda is a nice app with a nice community and is overall good the only problem is the UI is a bit complex but nice app
Birda. I like Birda to see sights of birds and interesting facts that I wouldn’t get the chance to see otherwise. Thanks!
Doesn’t even load.. All it does is take me to a page that says aww snap tell the developers

Love this app A very great choice. I’ve used the app for 4 months and it’s full of a great people who can identify a bird for you that you don’t know and you can share your sightings of those birds or you can just look at pictures. I recommend this app for people looking for a community full of birders

Birds. I like knowing what kind of bird is around me, if I don’t already know what kind of bird it might be. I also like knowing how these birds conquer a day without losing their lives within a day, I know these birds have to be brave too.:)!!!!

Really need a different way to location. The account creation bog that I reported before is now resolved, but I’m trying to log birds that I typically see in my neighborhood and I don’t want to create a precise location. Also, 400 m is not enough of a diameter. Maybe let us just log the county where we saw it? I won’t be filling in any sightings until I can create a location that doesn’t have me narrowed down to my pretty small town.

Great Concept, Questionable Execution. The birding community has long needed a dedicated social media app to bring us together and share stories, photos, and life lists. 

Unfortunately, with Birda it seems as though every feature that would allow this app to grow an online community is stuck behind a pay wall. 

This apps ability to keep records of your birding lists does not compare to the functionality an open source system such as eBird. However, it could act as a place for birders to come together that rivals apps such as Facebook if only basic features, such as your life list or ability to communicate with other birders, were not hidden behind paywalls. 

In sort, too many in-app purchases.

Nice. Love this app, it’s very beginner friendly and easy to use and was a huge help as I started to get into birding. EBird is definitely a bit more intimidating getting started. Also enjoy the social media style of it and the ability to post comments! Only gripe is there are a few species in my area that aren’t an option on Birda, and I don’t mean escapee/domestics, I mean like European Goldfinches and such. So I have to mark them as “unknown species” and hope I can go back and edit them someday in the future.

Best Birding App By Far. My wife and I have tried a host of apps, including Birfa and Ebird, and this is by far the best. Seeing EXACT locations where others spotted birds, making social media like posts to share your birding sessions and sighting, following other birders to always see their posts, and the artwork for each bird to help identify is beautiful. The app is super clean and easy to use. 10/10 recommend to any and every birder.

Makes my bird nerd self happy!. Love this app! I’m a beginner birder and starting birding because of this app. I’ve been learning much more things because of this app! Also, I gotta love the bird walk feature, it’s pretty cool. Really the only bad thing is that there isn’t a sound ID feature, but obviously you can just get Merlin ID for that. 

Overall, I totally recommend this app!

User Friendly. As a new birder I found a lot of things intimidating g other apps but Birda was beginner friendly, easy to use and fun. As a more experienced birder I now love all the stats and photos. Still my favorite bird watching app.
Birda is the word. Wonderful community and helpful staff. Has a little room for improvement but I’m enjoying it immensely.
Can’t get passed the address step. App won’t let me skip or add an address. Skip button doesn’t work and it doesn’t add an address. What a waste.

Doesn’t Work. Downloaded the app and could never get past setting my location. Tried to set my location multiple times. It just kept going back the main screen that told me to set my location and wouldn’t allow me to skip. Restarted the app, tried a different email, etc. Deleted the app, not worth the energy.

Login. I tried to log numerous times. When I try too create a new account it stop at the chose my location part I can’t get any farther then that. I have restarted my phone and redownloaded the app still the same thing

such a wonderful app. i don’t write reviews, but this little app is SO wonderful. i love how easy it is to use and all the features it has. the community is so fun to be apart of and it makes me want to get outside more often! i’ve always loved birds and birding, but this app has made birding even more enjoyable. would absolutely recommend.

Birda. This app is probably one of the best birding apps I’ve used.

 It has been extremely helpful when it comes to keeping a log of your finds and connecting with the birding community has been a delight. The team is super helpful and nice.

Thankyou

This is absolutely amazing. Alright Birda I got a short review for you. Birda has found me some people that like the same thing as me, and I get an app that’s like social media but it’s for the best hobby ever.
stupid. I CANT EVEN SCAN LIKE OTHER APPS SIMULAR TO THIS NOT BY U

My Favorite Birding App. I use this app every chance I can get when I go out birding, it is a wonderful birding community, everyone is so nice and helpful. This app truly brings people together just for the love of birds and I couldn’t ask for more.
Nice. Nice
love birda!. i love the community and getting to share photos with my friends and other birders. customer service is wonderful too!

Love it!. I really love using this app and keeping track of all the sightings I have. It’s easy to use and really positive. I just wish more people were into birding - it’s a real life scavenger hunt. The only suggestion I would have is maybe to include a chart that shows you by month which birds you’ve sighted, that way I can easily see which birds are visiting by season.

Love Birda!. I really enjoy using Birda. It’s a fun way to connect with the birding community and to get help with sightings, as well as learn more about them. I also really appreciate that you can get quality service for free.

Finally a Birding app for everyone!. Having used different birding apps for years daily, Birda has easily become my favorite! 
Birda has found a way to take key features from other birding apps, list keeping, a top tier bird guide, challenges, and plenty of educational features. 

The challenges are fun and unique to Birda! Which really does inspire you to get out and look for birds! You get “Badges” for completing challenges which is fun. You can also set your own challenges for you to complete! 

Seeing posts from people all over the world has been very educational.

The list keeping in this app is great! There are photos of the birds next to the name which is great for beginners but also great for experienced birders. Just a click from there and you are brought to a wealth of info on the bird, including the calls! And all within the app! Not only can you see your bird lists but see the amount of time you spent. 

The biggest appeal to me has been the social features that make it fun to really “bird nerd out” with other birders and bird watchers... I can only do that so much on other social apps. Here it’s a part of it.

Get Birding with Birda. Birda is perfect for all levels of birders. It is very user friendly . It includes guides for birds in your area so even if you do not recognize a bird you can still identify through their user friendly guide. If you are unable to decipher what bird you saw their is a feature where you can post your sighting of an unidentified species and the Birda community will help you figure out what bird you saw! Birda s challenges inspire you to go outside as each month they set a new goal for you to meet. Birda is the perfect birding app.

Amazing. I dont know what to say. The community is great, the features are great, no massive popup ads… I can’t get enough of it. It seems like even though there’s a diverse audience on Birda, everyone seems to get along great and have a lot of fun. You don’t have to tell everyone about who you are, or get into political matters or do anything stressful on Birda. It’s just an app where you can have fun outdoors and chat with a bunch of nice people that you don’t know but you sort of get to know in a way over time through the way they show themselves on the community. Overall, 10/10 app would recommend to birders of any skill level (being an extremely inexperienced birder myself 😅). Thanks for the great experience, Birda!

2 of 3 ducks not found listed in the app. I saw a female Australian shelduck (Tadorna tadornoides), a female ruddy shelduck (Tadorna ferruguinea) and some mallards 🦆in Durham, NC. The first 2 are not listed in the app, I had to create the sighting as unidentified species. I don’t know if it’s something related with the location, as these 2 are not normally seen in the US, but in Australia and Asia respectively.

Amazing idea but…. This app seems like an amazing idea…however, I just attempted to import my eBird data into Birda and discovered it is not a live sync. When I want this data to refresh in Birda I need to download my eBird data as a csv and then upload to Birda each time. I’m not leaving eBird and I don’t want to manually keep 2 checklist apps in sync. 

Sadly, I won’t use this app unless/until an eBird live sync is available…which other apps have.

Has potential, needs bug fixes. Has some potential! i’d like to see a few bugs fixed because I’ve only use the app for a few minutes and I’ve already found some glitches. 
Note to the devs: 
- “Nearby” should be set to a handful of miles or perhaps within your state, not several states over. That’s not really nearby. 
- Default view when you open the app should be the people you’re following, not Community. Most people will likely prefer to see what their friends are spotting or what is being seen nearby. 
- Overall, the app is very slow. Blank screens, long load times, etc. When you post a sighting, it takes a long time for it to register to your life list. I made multiple posts of the same sighting trying to get it to show up in my list. It did show up but much later…and so did the rest of my duplicate posts. 
Overall, the app has promise but is too buggy to enjoy right now.

Birda Nerda. I recently found Birda a few months ago and stoked about it! I love being able to catalog collections of things like my music collection, movies, etc.. and love how easy it is with Birda to log the birds I’ve seen. I’m not a social birder and enjoy it by my self or sometimes with my dad or my girlfriend. That being said, the social aspect of Birda I actually find fun! I enjoy seeing what people near and far from me are spotting. The most rad thing for me is earning all the different badges! A must download app for any birder of any skill level!

Favorite Birding App. I’m not a full time birder, but I’m a wildlife and nature photographer. I’ve decided over the past few years to get more into bird photography. 
I decided I wanted to keep track of the birds I’ve photographed as I went about it. I tried several other apps, and they were either too difficult or had to be paid for. 
This one is super easy, and there’s a lot of friendly people in this community. 
Only thing I would recommend is seeing if they could do a Sound ID thing like Merlin does so I could just use this app and that’s it.

Pleasant solution to more complex apps. This app is a gentle kindness. It works well, it has nice little features, and I feel happy when using it. The more scientific competitors like Merlin and eBird will always be the definitive resource for identification, but having a more intuitive catalogue and social component to birding is enjoyable. I had a small issue early on in using and the customer support chat was very helpful and pleasant

Great app.. I love Birda because it’s an accessible way to get into birding. I’m a die hard eBird user, but I understand it’s not for everyone. Especially those who feel a bit more casual about their birding activity. The great thing about Birda is that you still contribute to science.

Pleasant experience thus far, lovely app design and functionality.. Given the app’s social and photo posting functionality I’d love to see the ability to add “alt/descriptive text” to submissions as an Accessibility option for those with vision impairment or those utilizing screen readers.
Garbage. This app is garbage! 4 million sign up screens and no automated method of bird identification!

Nice way to engage with a community of birders. Birda is a great idea. It’s a birding app that connects curious people within a nature-centric, online community. Learning more about the natural world and sharing your findings with a community of likeminded folks is a really good place to start help folks value the biodiversity that we have. And begin to protect it, too.

Great app. A lot of fun and easy to use. It’s also informative. I hope, like E-Bird, they add rankings, as far as species seen, for world, state, county etc… Being able to add videos along with pictures would be nice too.

Ok. I can see the potential for this app, especially for new birders. The ‘gamification’ and badges etc might make for fun challenges for new and old birders. 
As someone who has been listing daily on eBird for years I am a lot more in tune with that app and record keeping style. Trying to use eBird with Merlin and then simultaneously keeping up with another similar app in the field is just too much and I personally find it too time consuming and distracting. I’ve given it a few weeks and realized it’s just one more thing I’m staring at on my phone when I should be concentrating on the birds and instead I’m staring at my phone trying to simultaneously keep two accurate lists with different types of data entry. 
I may try adding eBird data manually at the end of the week for a bit but eBird has the top billing for accurately maintaining my personal records in an easy to digest format. 
It’s a fun addition to the birding space and folks who aren’t big listers or eBird users will surely find it fun and valuable but it’s more of a novelty in my opinion. I do appreciate the effort to introduce another app to liven up birding.

Hope eBird is supported. For now users may import their eBird sitings which is slow & time consuming. Having used eBird for a decade I have no plans to abandon the app as I can submit observations effortlessly using 4 letter codes and use Siri to put in observations for me while driving. I hope a feed from eBird is added soon as I will likely only "import" once a year. - You can see local sightings, which is really helpful.

- You can’t record more than one bird if you are just entering a sighting. Sometimes I see a few on the bird feeder and would like to add multiple species and numbers of each species.
